verdict.rationale: DBOS's docs repeatedly describe the core durable-workflow library as open source, and its source is published in a public GitHub repo (dbos-inc/dbos-transact-py). A community report says the web UI (Conductor/console) is not open source, so only part of the product's source is readable. missing for 10: the specific open-source license named in evidence, open-source availability of the Conductor/console web UI, and independent corroboration of licensing terms.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license

citations.quote: The open-source DBOS library uses Postgres to orchestrate durable workflows and queues.
DBOS is an open-source Postgres-backed library. To add DBOS to an application, you install the open-source library and annotate workflows and steps.
you can use DBOS to add durable workflows and queues to your program in just a few lines of code.
